subject: Chemistry
topic: Trends in standard electrode potentials of 3d metals
title: Zinc Fizzes, Copper Stays Silent: Electrode Potentials of the 3d Metals
summary: Copper is the only 3d metal with a positive E°(M²⁺/M) (+0.34 V), so it gives no H₂ with dilute acids. Turning Cu(s) into Cu²⁺(aq) costs more (atomisation + two ionisations) than hydration pays back: 921 against zinc's 711 kJ/mol. Stable d⁵ and d¹⁰ bend the trend: Mn and Zn dip, Mn³⁺ is a strong oxidant, Fe³⁺ is stable.

notes.title: 07 – Trends in Standard Electrode Potentials of the 3d Metals

keyPoints: **More negative E°(M²⁺/M)** = the metal forms M²⁺(aq) more easily; metals below 0 V give **H₂** with dilute acids.
**Copper alone is positive (+0.34 V)**: no H₂ from dilute acids, though **oxidising acids** (nitric, hot conc. sulphuric) dissolve it.
**Energy bill** M(s) → M²⁺(aq) = atomisation + IE₁ + IE₂ + hydration: **Zn 711**, **Cu 921 kJ/mol** (NCERT Table 4.4).
**Stable d⁵ / d¹⁰**: Mn and Zn are more negative than the trend; **Mn³⁺** (→ d⁵) is a strong oxidant (+1.57 V); **Fe³⁺** is already d⁵ (+0.77 V).

blocks.p: Copper's costs (atomisation and the second ionisation) are much higher, and its hydration enthalpy cannot make up for them, so E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) is positive. Across the series the net bill follows the E° order (Mn 643, Zn 711, Fe 743, Ni 798, Cu 921).

list: Mn²⁺ (d⁵) and Zn²⁺ (d¹⁰) are especially stable: E° of Mn and Zn are more negative than the trend (Ni too, because of its high hydration enthalpy).
E°(Mn³⁺/Mn²⁺) = +1.57 V: Mn³⁺ gains a stable d⁵ by taking one electron, so it is a strong oxidising agent.
E°(Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺) = +0.77 V, comparatively low: Fe³⁺ is already d⁵.
Co³⁺/Co²⁺ = +1.97 V: Co³⁺ is also strongly oxidising.

quiz.q: The only 3d metal with a positive E°(M²⁺/M):

quiz.explain: An oxidising acid; no H₂ is given.

quiz.q: Net bill for Cu(s) → Cu²⁺(aq), NCERT data:
Mn³⁺ is a strong oxidising agent because:
quiz.explain: Taking one electron gives half-filled d⁵.

simulation.reason: The idea is a sum of four tabulated energies compared across metals; the worked Zn and Cu bills and the table teach it fully, and varying a metal would add nothing beyond the table.
